Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

SIMPLIFIED PRESENTATION u ftfcVrFt&*^ i »* u 



1. Scope — Prescribes method of simplified representations of some of the basic features 
drawings. 



on 



2. The dimension, lines and extension lines belonging to representation of holes, counterbores, 
threads and bolt or rivet fastenings can be replaced by leaders running from the representations to 
the dimensions or designations (for example, thread symbol and code designations). If these 
representations are too small and are thus not clear, they may be omitted. In their place centre 
lines are used and where centre line crosses the leaders should be drawn to the dimensions and 
designation. 

3. Leaders should always begin at that point (side) on which the holes, thread counterbores or 
components lie or from which the components are introduced and be drawn towards that side and 
provided with designations, in the sequence in which assembly is carried out. With hidden holes 
or components, the leaders, insofar as they are hidden, should be drawn as broken lines ( to be 
avoided as far as possible, in cases of doubt add a note : 'introduced from below or below. )' 

4. The IS designations of the components, as far as possible, be abbreviated where the organization 
concerned has adopted this practice; they should however remain clear. The name, for example, may 
be omitted. 

Example :

i ) The dimensions '5 deep and 10 deep' relate to the usable depth of thread [see 4.3.9.10 
and Fig 4.83 of IS : 696-1972 'Code of practice for general engineering drawings 
( second revision )' ]. It is also necessary to give the depth of the holes in drawing. Thus 
the information given in Fig 10 is, for example, of M 3-5/7 deep.

EXPLANATORY NOTE 

Representation of basic standard features like holes, CSK holes, CBR holes, etc, which normally 
require execution of intricate details by drawing can be simplified by giving reference to the location 
of the features or the centre line using a leader line at the end of which designations of the standard 
features are indicated. Thus considerable saving in draughting time is achieved without impairing the 
communication. This can be further extended to threaded fasteners, rivets, etc. 

This standard is based on and is in conformity with DIN 30-1970 'Drawings, simplified 
presentations'.
